data.title: Fizzy Lemon Volcano
data.description: Mix baking soda and lemon juice to discover exciting signs of a chemical reaction like fizzing and bubbling!

experiment.name: Lemon Juice and Baking Soda Volcano
experiment.realWorldConnection: This is very similar to how baking powder helps fluffy cakes rise in your oven when mixed with wet ingredients!

substances.name: Baking Soda
substances.safetyInfo: Do not taste. Wash hands after handling.
substances.imagePrompt: A pile of white powder on a spoon

substances.name: Lemon Juice
substances.imagePrompt: Fresh yellow lemon juice in a clear glass cup

reaction.particleDescription: When the lemon juice touches the baking soda, their tiny particles smash together, breaking old bonds and creating brand-new gas particles that escape into the air as bubbly foam!

challenges.instruction: Why did the mixture suddenly bubble up and fizz when the two substances met?
challenges.targetAnswer: The substances swapped partners and created a brand-new gas.
challenges.hint: Think about what happened to the particles when they touched.
challenges.narration: Fantastic job thinking like a real scientist! You uncovered how mixing two things can unleash invisible gases.

options.text: The particles rearranged themselves and formed bubbles of new gas.
The lemon juice simply painted the white powder yellow.
The baking soda melted from the wetness of the juice.
Air from the room got trapped inside the spoon.

challenges.instruction: True or False: Even though gas floated away into the air, the total amount of matter is still conserved during the reaction.
challenges.hint: Matter doesn't disappear; it just changes form!
challenges.narration: You are mastering the secrets of the universe! Matter always accounts for itself.

notebook.predictPrompt: What do you think will happen when we pour lemon juice onto the white baking soda powder?

predictionOptions.text: It will start bubbling, fizzing, and foaming up.
It will turn into a solid rock.
It will glow brightly in the dark.

observePrompts: What did you see happen right after the liquids and solids mixed?
Did you hear any sounds during the experiment?
Did the cup feel warmer, colder, or stay the same?
notebook.explainPrompt: How do you know for sure that a chemical reaction took place here?

data.imagePrompt: A fun science experiment with a cup, foaming fizz, lemon slices, and baking soda on a wooden table
